assessmentSummary.identity: A two-variant bilateral quadruped hand-pressure family requiring explicit variant selection. Finger Pulses keep both palms, fingers, and knees supported while pressure through the fingers and flexed first knuckles deliberately increases then releases without bouncing. Palm Lifts keep fingers, distal or top palms, and knees supported while both palm heels lift and lower under control. One complete pressure increase and release or palm-heel lift and lower is one repetition. Pace, comfortable range, body-mass distribution, repetitions, sets, rest, and stable knee cushioning are delivery annotations. Seated, standing-fold, tall-plank, raised-support, unilateral, finger-lift, knuckle-roll, wrist-rock, hold, loaded, manual, or clinical tasks require another reviewed identity.
currentCardFindings: Source 32 has one combined skeletal variant and generic profile with empty controlled taxonomy, anatomy, load, fatigue, constraints, support, research, alternate, calibration, and exact media review data.
The legacy card combines Finger Pulses and Palm Lifts even though the direct source numbers and describes them as separate actions with different retained contacts.
Legacy age, publication, broad outcome, and reviewed-media implications are unsupported and must be cleared or quarantined.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when one exact action, quadruped base, required hand and knee contacts, comfortable finger, knuckle, palm and wrist support, clean surface, low dose, duration, symptoms, and downstream finger, grip and hand-support budgets fit. Do not switch variants silently, force pressure or height, add a different base, finger lift, knuckle roll, wrist rock, hold, support height, resistance, or assessment. Choose a separately authored card when that changed task is intended.

currentCardSnapshot.description: A two-variant bilateral quadruped hand-pressure family that requires explicit variant selection. Finger Pulses keep both palms and fingers supported while pressure through the fingers and flexed first knuckles increases and decreases without bouncing. Palm Lifts keep the fingers and distal or top palm supported while both palm heels lift and lower under control. One pressure increase and release is one finger pulse; one palm-heel lift and controlled lower is one palm-lift repetition. Base, action, contacts, and count may not be mixed. Pace, comfortable range, repetitions, sets, rest, and stable knee cushioning are delivery annotations. Seated or standing support, tall plank, unilateral work, finger lifts, knuckle rolling, wrist rocking, holds, resistance, manual force, or assessment changes the task.

claims: GMB separately describes finger pressure with first knuckles bent and palm-heel lifting with fingers and the distal hand retained on the floor.
Model the observable hand contacts and actions; do not claim measured muscle activation, quantified force, one universal joint angle, or isolated tissue targeting.
The two numbered tasks have different contact and action requirements but the source supplies no Vortex difficulty scores.
Finger Pulse 24/18/24 and Palm Lift 28/22/28 are review-only exercise-complexity, physical-difficulty, and derived-maximum proposals; they never classify a participant.

evidence.sourcePublisher: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
claims: Gymnastics wrist angle and moment vary with hand-support conditions, but back-handspring findings cannot be converted into force or pressure values for these low-load actions.

Track exact repetitions, finger-pressure, palm-lift, wrist-support and hand-support seconds, required contacts, faults, symptoms, and overlapping same-session grip and hand-support work; recovery remains a planning estimate.

evidence.sourceTitle: Epidemiology and Risk Factors of Wrist Pain and Injury in Adolescent Artistic Gymnasts: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
claims: The review reports substantial wrist-pain and injury burden in adolescent gymnastics with low-to-very-low certainty for available risk-factor evidence; it does not create an age rule or authorize exercise through symptoms.

Selection requires safe floor entry, comfortable selected hand contacts, clean stable surface, communication, symptom monitoring, and compatible finger, wrist, grip, and downstream hand-support exposure.
USA Gymnastics says to seek medical guidance when pain is present, discontinue exercises that cause pain, and reduce work when form breaks down.
Stop for pain, skin injury, neurologic or circulation symptoms, dizziness, worsening discomfort, required-contact loss, forced or bouncing action, unsafe surface, or participant request.
GMB places both tasks early in an optional wrist routine and says Finger Pulse repetitions depend on current feeling and upcoming work.
Use low-volume quality-first Prepare & Access or Movement Intelligence profiles and recompute hand, wrist, grip, duration, technical-fatigue, and downstream hand-support budgets.
GMB gives distinct short instructions for pressure through fingers without bouncing and for palm-heel lifting with fingers and distal hand retained down.
Athlete support must name one exact variant, show which contacts stay down, define one complete pressure-release or lift-lower count, and provide a clear stop and help signal.
The GMB sheet pairs each numbered action with separate close hand images and concise text.

Provide close-up and side demonstrations, separate two-frame count cards, slower pace, fewer repetitions, more rest, optional stable knee cushioning, and a separately authored task when floor contact does not fit.

GMB numbers Finger Pulses and Palm Pulses as separate exercises and gives each a different action and contact description.
Source 32 remains a stable family wrapper but requires explicit exact variant selection; the combined baseline is not selectable.
Both tasks use supported hands and active pressure control rather than bodyweight wrist rocking.
Use controlled brace and push patterns; activation and preparation are contextual purposes rather than invented movement-pattern keys.

claims: Wrist angle and moment vary with gymnastics support conditions, demonstrating that exact contact and support details matter.
The study examines back handsprings, not these tasks, so the card records observable contacts, action, range, support time, and symptoms without importing force values.
GMB gives 10-30 Finger Pulse repetitions depending on current feeling and work ahead but supplies no Palm Pulse dose.
Use a conservative review-only one-to-two sets of five-to-twelve exact repetitions, calculate actual support time, and stop before contact, pressure, support, or symptom quality degrades.
GMB supports pressure through fingers with first knuckles bent without bouncing and separately supports palm lifting with fingers and the distal hand retained down.
The card adds exact quadruped base, bilateral contacts, complete-return counting, clean stable surface, symptom stops, and actual-dose recording.

evidence.sourceTitle: Epidemiology and Risk Factors of Wrist Pain and Injury in Adolescent Artistic Gymnasts: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
claims: The systematic review supports taking gymnastics wrist symptoms and accumulated exposure seriously while emphasizing low certainty and absent training thresholds.

Coach support verifies selected action, floor entry, hand contacts, finger, palm and wrist tolerance, upper-body support, first fault, actual exposure, downstream demand, and escalation without diagnosis.
GMB separates Finger Pulses, Palm Pulses, Side-to-Side Palm Rotations, wrist stretches, and elbow rotations.

Keep changed bases, laterality, finger lifts, knuckle rolls, wrist rocks, holds, support heights, external force, manual work, and assessments outside the two exact variants until separately authored and reviewed.

alternateAssessments.name: Finger Pulses, Finger Pressure Pulses, or Quadruped Finger Pulses
alternateAssessments.rationale: Aliases fit only when bilateral quadruped whole-hand contact and one pressure increase and release are exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Palm Pulses, Palm Lifts, or Palm-Heel Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Aliases fit only when bilateral quadruped fingers and distal palms stay down during one palm-heel lift and lower.

alternateAssessments.name: Smaller Pressure or Palm-Heel Height
alternateAssessments.rationale: Comfortable pressure or lift range changes dose while action, contacts, and return remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Tempo, Repetitions, Sets, or Rest
alternateAssessments.rationale: Pace, volume, and recovery change dose rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Stable Knee Cushioning
alternateAssessments.rationale: Knee cushioning changes comfort without changing hand contact, base, or action.

alternateAssessments.name: Comfortable Hand Spacing or Finger Spread
alternateAssessments.rationale: Spacing changes setup within comfort while forward orientation, action, contacts, and count remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Body-Mass Shift Back Within Quadruped
alternateAssessments.rationale: Shifting mass back reduces pressure only when knees, contacts, action, and count remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Seated Finger Pulses or Palm Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Removing quadruped knee and trunk support changes bodyweight transfer, floor access, load, and setup.

alternateAssessments.name: Standing Forward-Fold Finger Pulses
alternateAssessments.rationale: Standing support changes balance, posterior-chain range, floor entry, load, and failure consequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Tall-Plank Finger Pulses or Palm Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Toe support and long leverage materially increase hand, wrist, shoulder, trunk, and fatigue demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Raised-Support Finger Pulses or Palm Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Raised support changes equipment, height, load, angles, station, and failure consequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Unilateral Finger Pulse or Palm Lift
alternateAssessments.rationale: One-hand emphasis changes laterality, load distribution, trunk demand, and failure consequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Side-to-Side Palm Rotations or Knuckle Rolls
alternateAssessments.rationale: Rolling pressure along the knuckles adds a lateral path, checkpoints, and asymmetrical contact.

alternateAssessments.name: Palm Press Finger Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Lifting fingers while the palm remains supported reverses the moving contact and changes action and loading.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Rockers — Palms Down
alternateAssessments.rationale: Whole-palmar support with bodyweight rocking changes action, range, count, and loading direction.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Rockers — Backs of Hands Down
alternateAssessments.rationale: Dorsal-hand support and wrist-flexion rocking change hand surface, action, range, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Lean Isometric or Wrist Support Rock Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A sustained endpoint or longer-lever support changes count, duration, load, purpose, and fatigue.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Wrist Pronation-Supination Shifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Changing hand orientation adds forearm rotation and multiple directional exposures.

alternateAssessments.name: Loaded, Banded, or Partner-Resisted Hand Pulses
alternateAssessments.rationale: External or manual force changes magnitude, direction, equipment, consent, failure risk, and scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Clinical Finger, Wrist, or Hand-Pressure Assessment
alternateAssessments.rationale: Measurement adds examiner protocol, clinical purpose, outcomes, consent, and different escalation.
